title: Lower Respiratory Tract Infection — Follow-up
text: For adults with productive cough and fever lasting under 7 days without red-flag signs (breathlessness at rest, SpO2<94%, chest pain), manage symptomatically, review in 3-5 days, and reassess if fever persists beyond 3 days on treatment. Avoid penicillin-class antibiotics in patients with a documented penicillin allergy; prefer a macrolide or as locally indicated.

title: Post-Discharge Cardiac Follow-up
text: Patients with known coronary artery disease reporting exertional chest tightness require urgent risk re-stratification: 12-lead ECG, troponin if available, and same-week cardiology review. Continue existing antiplatelet and antihypertensive therapy unless contraindicated. Educate on red-flag symptoms requiring emergency care: rest pain, diaphoresis, radiating pain, syncope.

title: Pediatric Sore Throat Management
text: In children with sore throat and low-grade fever under 3 days, assess for Centor-type criteria (tonsillar exudate, tender nodes, absence of cough, fever). If antibiotics are indicated and the child has a documented amoxicillin/penicillin allergy, use a non-beta-lactam alternative and confirm the allergy history with a caregiver before prescribing. Advise return if difficulty breathing, drooling, or inability to swallow fluids develops.

title: CKD Stage 3 Routine Follow-up
text: For CKD Stage 3 patients on ACE inhibitor/ARB therapy presenting with new mild peripheral edema, check renal function (creatinine, eGFR) and electrolytes, review sodium intake, and monitor blood pressure. Avoid nephrotoxic NSAIDs and sulfonamide-containing drugs where there is a documented sulfa allergy. Escalate to nephrology if eGFR has dropped more than 25% from baseline or edema worsens.

title: Type 2 Diabetes — Routine Monitoring
text: Patients on stable metformin therapy should have HbA1c reviewed every 3 months and be screened for gastrointestinal side effects. Metformin should be used cautiously if renal function is impaired (eGFR<30 is a contraindication). Reinforce dietary carbohydrate counting and physical activity at every follow-up.

title: Allergy Conflict Escalation Rule
text: Any proposed medication that matches a patient's documented allergy list must never be finalized automatically. The follow-up plan must be routed to a human clinician for review with the conflict explicitly flagged, and an alternative class of medication should be suggested where clinically reasonable.
